rfc_version: DRAFT 2026-10-11 (pre-RFC; the RFC text lands with T05-7a)

generated_by.tool: python3 stdlib generator (BCS, SHA-256, RFC 8032 Ed25519 from scratch; self-tested on RFC 8032 §7.1 and on contracts vector V-08)
generated_by.note: Written by the same author as the Rust code, without sharing code with it. The independent oracle (T13-2) has not reproduced these vectors yet.

frame: u32 little-endian length, then BCS(ReceiptV1) = BCS(ReceiptBodyV1) followed by the 64-byte signature; length 1..=1024

checks.rule: A frame header or body runs past the end of the log.
The frame length is 0 or above 1024, or the frame is not exactly the canonical BCS of a ReceiptV1.
signer_key differs from the pinned key or, with no pinned key, from the first receipt's.
Strict RFC 8032 Ed25519 verification of the signature over tagged_digest(VAULTEX/RECEIPT/v1, body) fails: canonical S, and no small-order public key or R.
seq is not the next position: 0 for the first receipt, or the checkpoint's seq + 1.
prev is not the previous receipt's digest (all zeros at seq 0, or the checkpoint digest).
time_s is lower than the previous receipt's (equal is allowed).
The network is not a network of the receipt's chain.
An accept carries no intent digest.
policy_version is lower than the previous receipt's, or equal with a different policy_digest.

vectors.description: A receipt log written by one key: an accept (the first receipt of a chain, identical to contracts vector V-08), a decoder refusal without an intent, and a policy refusal with a rule index whose caller clock ran behind.

steps.note: Accept: the contracts v0 TRC-20 vector. Identical to contracts vector V-08.
Refusal by the decoder (the TRC-20 vector with a memo): no intent.
Refusal by policy rule 0 (the native vector); the caller's clock is 0.5 s behind the previous receipt, so the time is held at the previous receipt's.

vectors.description: The log of A-001, verified against the pinned receipt key.
The same log with no pinned key: the first receipt's key is adopted, and the result says the key was not pinned.
A segment: receipts 1 and 2, verified from a checkpoint (seq 0 and its digest).
An empty log is valid and has no head.
A log cut at a receipt boundary is a valid prefix: dropped receipts at the end cannot be detected without an anchored head (KI-16).
A frame that ends past the end of the log (a torn write).
Receipt 2's frame holds one byte after the receipt, so it is not the canonical encoding.
A frame header with length 0.
The pinned key is a different key.
Receipt 2 is signed by a different key (correct seq and link), with no pinned key: the key changes inside the log.
Receipt 1's body is altered (refusal code) after signing.
One bit of receipt 1's signature is flipped.
Receipt 1 is signed under another domain tag (VAULTEX/APPROVAL/v1) by the right key.
Receipt 1's signature with S + L (a non-canonical scalar): rejected by strict verification.
Receipt 1 signed by the right key with a small-order R (it satisfies the cofactorless equation): rejected by strict verification.
A one-receipt log whose key is a small-order point (the identity), with R = identity and S = 0, and no pinned key: rejected by strict verification.
A duplicated sequence number: receipt 1 appears twice.
A reordered chain: receipts 0, 2, 1.
A log that starts at seq 1 without a checkpoint.
A broken link: receipt 2 names receipt 0's digest as prev.
A segment checked against the wrong checkpoint digest.
Receipt 2's time is one second before receipt 1's.
Receipt 2 names a TRON network under the EVM chain code.
Receipt 1 (no intent) is an accept.
Receipt 2's policy version is lower than receipt 1's.
Receipt 2 names policy version 1 with a different digest.
